books.name: fsent_champ_long_htf15_htffs
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - FAILS THE DRAWDOWN BUDGET, and is registered with that stated first because it is the arm that looks best on a net column and is disqualified by a single number. fsent_champ_long_htf15 with exp_htf_fs_entry='flip'. WHY IT IS NOT THE PICK: in-sample drawdown 29.62R is OVER the owner's 29R ceiling, before any consideration of the return. It also re-creates a negative half-year that its own parent does not have (htf15 has 0, this has 1), so it fails the zero-negative rule twice over. The period control passes - b = +1.05 at t = +3.29 on the half-year fixed effect, better in 5 of 6 years - so the gain itself is not a period artifact; it is the risk it carries that disqualifies it. Registered because it is the highest in-sample net measured anywhere in the fsent family, +925.79R, and burying the number that beats every other one while omitting the ceiling it breaches is the failure mode this family has been guarding against all cycle. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0105 in sample, p = 0.4904 out of sample, gap +392.43R IS and +64.58R OOS. THE STRONGEST IN-SAMPLE RESULT IN THE ENTIRE FAMILY, and not significant out of sample. Stating that pair next to each other is the point: a p of 0.0105 on its own is the number a person would quote, and the 0.4904 beside it is the number that decides. It is disqualified on the drawdown ceiling before either of them is consulted, but if that ceiling were lifted it would still be an in-sample-only result.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_htfesmcl4
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the largest-return arm measured in this family, and registered because the owner asked for every arm to be visible rather than pre-filtered. It stacks the HTF-side FS entry (exp_htf_fs_entry=all) with max_consecutive_losses=4, which is the one setting that clears the 2022-H2 cell that the FS entry alone re-broke. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 793t / +917.80R / DD 27.74R / WR 43.0%, OOS 437t / +326.22R / DD 14.20R / WR 37.8%. (1) In-sample drawdown 27.74R is at the owner's 29R budget ceiling, against 15.13R for fsent_champ_long_mcloff on less than half the return. (2) PERIOD CONTROL IS UNDERPOWERED OUT OF SAMPLE - b = +0.027 with t = 0.05 and MDE 1.16, i.e. the out-of-sample effect is indistinguishable from nothing, and the cluster bootstrap goes NEGATIVE at -0.03. (3) The FS entry collapses the flip/decisive/b2 regime buckets into one fs_entered set, so this arm stops distinguishing regimes - see method/HTF_FS_ENTRY_REJECTED.md. It buys +384R of in-sample return mostly by admitting 528 new trades rather than by improving the ones it had. Registered as the high-return end of the range so the owner can see what the ceiling costs. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0285 in sample, p = 0.5311 out of sample, gap +384.44 IS and +86.63 OOS - significant in sample, NOT out of sample. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). books.name: fsent_champ_long_htffs
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the strongest arm in this family on the owner's own rule, and the first one that adds return without adding a negative half-year. ONE parameter from the shipping book: exp_htf_fs_entry='flip', so the HTF flip-bucket window opens on the swing's FS print instead of on the break, while the decisive and b2 buckets keep their breaks. That is the selective form of the arm rejected on 2026-10-09 - 'all' was rejected partly because it collapsed flip/decisive/b2 into one fs_both set and the book stopped distinguishing regimes; this keeps two of the three intact. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 770t / +897.94R / DD 19.78R / WR 42.3%, OOS 415t / +300.43R / DD 14.35R / WR 36.9%. That is +364.57R in sample and +60.84R out of sample on 242 more trades. THE OWNER'S RULE: drawdown 19.78R is inside the 29R budget, and the negative half-year count is UNCHANGED at 1 - this arm does not bring back the 2025-H1 cell that htf_fs='all' re-broke, which is the specific failure that sank the earlier test. PERIOD CONTROL PASSES BOTH WAYS: with a calendar-year fixed effect b = +1.34 at t = +3.24, and with the stricter half-year fixed effect b = +1.40 at t = +3.40, better in 5 of 6 years. It is also the largest gain the half-year test has ever survived in this family. CAUSALITY IS CLEAN, measured in HTF_FS_ENTRY_REJECTED.md: window_start minus its own FS print is exactly 0.0h at min, median and max in both eras, and zero entries precede their window_start - an FS-anchored window opens precisely at the print, not before it. WHAT IT COSTS: the same objection that applies to every FS-entered window applies here - 95% of the gain sits in 197 windows the book was not trading before, trades per window roughly doubles, and the drawdown goes from 13.42R to 19.78R. The return is real and survives a period control, but it is bought with breadth rather than with a better read of the existing windows, and it is bought with 46% more drawdown than the parent. Nothing is adopted: the 2021-22 era is reused old data, not a holdout. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0272 in sample, p = 0.5956 out of sample, gap +364.57R IS and +60.84R OOS - significant IN SAMPLE ONLY. The in-sample result is the strongest of its shape in this family and the out-of-sample one is not distinguishable from a reshuffle of the parent. So the honest ranking is unchanged by this arm: fsent_champ_long_mcloff remains the only book that clears in BOTH eras (0.0312 / 0.0117), and htf15_htffs' in-sample p of 0.0105 is the single lowest in-sample figure measured anywhere in the family paired with an out-of-sample figure of 0.4904. That pattern - very strong in sample, flat out of it - is exactly what the forward window exists to distinguish, and it is the reason +364R is not a recommendation.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_htf15_tskip6
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - fsent_champ_long_htf15 with exp_trail_skip_n=6, the strongest of the two verified skip_n books and the one where the risk improvement is largest. Same mechanism as fsent_champ_long_tskip4 and the same reason it is real: exp_trail_skip_n drops the first N trailing-stop events (unified.py:1493), converting weak early trail exits into ordinary stop exits at exactly -1.000R. Purging every stop-exit trade RAISES the net rather than lowering it (+723.83 -> +958.83 at skip_n=5), which is the opposite of a right-tail bet and is the test that killed swing shape, volatile candles and mark continuation. MEASURED, on the registry net lens (equity_quality): IS 412t / +639.84R / dd_net 22.81R / WR 40.8%, OOS 224t / +328.54R / dd_net 14.90R / WR 36.6%. MaxConsecL 13 IS / 11 OOS on the gross curve. Against the parent: +134.60R IS and +73.73R OOS, with IS drawdown IMPROVING 21.05 -> 18.09 and, uniquely among these books, THE WORST LOSING STREAK FALLING 22 -> 13 in sample and holding at 11 out of sample. The parent's OOS streak is 11 and this book's is 11, so nothing is traded away on the owner's stated first priority. WHY 6. Chosen on risk, not on the net argmax: skip_n=32 posts +875.80R IS but its OOS is +218.70 against the parent's +254.81 - it LOSES - and its IS DD is 26.65 with an OOS DD of 27.00. The DD-safe window here is 2..6, wider than the parent's 3..6, and 6 is the best net inside it. The value ladder is genuinely still rising past the value chosen, which is the honest reason not to push further: this is the top of the safe window, not a plateau, and the next rung costs drawdown. OOS WAS READ ONCE at the IS-selected value. CAVEAT CARRIED: OOS drawdown rises 9.98 -> 12.98. The in-sample drawdown gain does not carry out of sample; the losing streak and the net do. fsent_champ_short is out of scope by owner ruling. fsent_champ_long_htffs is deliberately NOT registered: its only DD-safe value is skip_n=2 and that LOSES on OOS (+281.75 against the parent's +313.35), and its +2570R at skip_n=32 costs DD 12.86 -> 30.05 and MaxConsecL 12 -> 23.

books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the best NON-degenerate arm found, and the two findings that actually changed the picture, stacked. It is fsent_champ_long_mcloff (max_consecutive_losses=0) on the htf15 1h swing series. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 560t / +616.17R / DD 15.13R / WR 41.1%, OOS 299t / +277.35R / DD 13.64R / WR 38.1%. It beats the parent in BOTH eras by more than mcloff alone (+82.80R IS, +37.76R OOS) and beats mcloff in both eras as well (+49.59R IS, +6.44R OOS), for 1.00R of extra in-sample drawdown. ZERO negative half-years out of 12. WHY THIS IS THE RECOMMENDATION AND NOT htf15 OR htfesmcl4: it does not use exp_htf_fs_entry, so it keeps the flip/decisive/b2 regime buckets distinct and is NOT the degenerate all-fs_entered configuration that the completion sweep's highest arms all turn out to be. The 12-arm joint grid over max_consecutive_losses x HTF leg length x HTF FS entry produced a +1321.41R arm, and that arm collapses the regime distinction - see method/HTF_FS_ENTRY_REJECTED.md. This one reaches +616.17R while staying honest about what a regime is. PERIOD CONTROL, run on this exact combination on 2026-10-09: SURVIVES with b > 0 in 2 of 2 eras - b = +0.77 (t = 1.72, MDE 0.88) IS and b = +0.62 (t = 1.60, MDE 0.76) OOS, cluster bootstraps +0.80 and +0.64 - but it is UNDERPOWERED, and this is the honest cost of the extra swing. fsent_champ_long_mcloff on its own is the only arm in the family whose control is powered in BOTH eras, at t = 3.37 and t = 3.97. Adding the htf15 swing buys +49.59R IS and dilutes the cohort variance at the same time, so the recommendation on EVIDENCE remains mcloff and the recommendation on RETURN is this one. Still NOT adopted: no arm in the family has forward evidence, and 12 observations of a half-year table is not a guarantee. See method/RESEARCH_COMPLETE.md and method/GRID_PERIOD_AND_KNOB_GUARD.md. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0115 in sample, p = 0.1445 out of sample, gap +82.80 IS and +37.76 OOS - significant in sample, NOT out of sample - the era that matters. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_tskip4
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - fsent_champ_long with exp_trail_skip_n=4, and the first result in this repo whose edge was CONFIRMED BY MECHANISM rather than by a net that survived OOS. exp_trail_skip_n drops the first N trailing-stop events outright (unified.py:1493, _trail_skip_rem -= 1; _tr_ok = False). WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, and this is the part worth reading: it does NOT improve exits on the same trades, it CONVERTS trail exits into stop exits. On the parent, 497 of 497 trades exit on the trail and ZERO hit the stop; at skip_n=5 it inverts to 185 trail and 244 SL. So the knob is turning trailing stops off for the first few moves, and positions that would have closed early at a small profit instead ride until the stop. EVERY one of those converted trades exits at exactly -1.000R - median and 10th percentile identical - so they are ordinary losses, not oversized ones, and they are the same weak trades the trail was closing for scraps. THE PURGE TEST IS WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM THE FOUR HYPOTHESES THAT DIED BEFORE IT. At the pin there is nothing to purge, because almost nothing exits on the stop. Above skip_n=4 the stop population is large, and removing every stop-exit trade RAISES the net on all three books tested (+616 -> +860 on long, +724 -> +959 on htf15, +1505 -> +1834 on htffs). A right-tail bet loses exactly that way, because its gain lives in the trades the filter removes. Here the survivors go from -0.20 to +2.31 median R. That is selection, not variance. MEASURED, on the registry net lens (equity_quality, which is what these pins use): IS 447t / +530.42R / dd_net 23.66R / WR 41.2%, OOS 240t / +260.53R / dd_net 15.49R / WR 40.0%. Against the parent that is +63.50R IS and +45.21R OOS, and the IS DRAWDOWN IMPROVES, 19.57 -> 17.99. WHY 4 AND NOT 5. The value was chosen on the owner's stated priority - drawdown and losing streak first - not on the net argmax. skip_n=32 posts +974.53R on IS, nearly double, and holds on OOS at +416.23R; it is rejected because its DD is 22.24 against the parent's 19.57 and its OOS DD is 26.44 against 9.85. The DD-safe window on this book is 3,4,5,6 and 4 is the best net inside it. OOS WAS READ ONCE, at the value IS selected, which is the discipline the last three hypotheses all failed. WHAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS: OOS drawdown RISES, 9.85 -> 12.05. The IS drawdown gain does not carry out of sample; what carries is the net and the losing streak. If OOS drawdown matters equally, skip_n=3 is the only value free on both eras (+230.92R OOS at DD 10.53) and it is the smaller prize. OWNER SCOPE: fsent_champ_short was ruled out of this work by the owner on 2026-10-14 and is deliberately NOT registered - short loses at every skip_n above 2, so the knob is not a family rule. THE SHORTCUT THAT WAS CORRECTED HERE, because it is the one this repo keeps making: the first census swept skip_n in {0,1,2,3,5}, found 5 best on all three books, and that is a BOUNDARY ARTEFACT - 5 was the top of the grid. Extended to 32 the IS argmax is 32 on all three books, and htf15 at 32 LOSES on OOS. The census number was never a promotion and was not treated as one.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_htf15
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the only arm found so far that fixes the shipping book's one negative half-year WITHOUT losing return, and it does so by moving a knob almost nobody has touched: the HTF swing length. THIS IS THE ONE FROM THE OWNER'S OWN RULE. Asked on 2026-10-09 for something that never goes negative - 'kabhi negative nahi hona chahiye' - the sweep of the HTF plane (1h swings, min_bars 10 -> 3..40) found that fsent_champ_long's single negative half-year, 2025-H1 at -0.7R, disappears at min_bars 13 and the net RISES from +773.0R to +796.5R (14) and +822.4R (15). MEASURED: IS 520t / +567.57R / DD 17.28R / WR 41.2%, OOS 280t / +254.88R / DD 16.86R / WR 37.1%. Against the parent that is +34.2R IS and +15.3R OOS on 8 and 31 fewer trades. WHY THIS IS NOT A GRID PEAK: the region around it is a genuine plateau, not a spike. min_bars 12 gives +783.5R but still 1 negative cell; 13 gives +787.6R with 0; 14 +796.5R with 0; 15 +822.4R with 0; 16 +746.1R with 0; 18 falls back to +708.7R with 1 negative again. By contrast min_bars 30 posts the single best number in the whole sweep at +847.3R with 0 negative - and is a SPIKE: 24 gives +645.4R with 2 negatives, 28 gives +659.6R with 2, 32 gives +696.3R with 0, 34 gives +562.5R. A 200R peak with a 60R trough either side is not an edge, so 30 is rejected and 15 is kept. WHAT CHANGED MECHANICALLY: the HTF plane is engine slot 2 and its swing series feeds the leg ratio, the bias-momentum breaks, the bias flips and _sw_ts_dir_mag, which is the flip/decisive classification every trade is tagged with. A longer 1h leg means fewer, larger HTF windows - 1601 swings at min_bars 10 down to 1479 at 15 - so the regime the router sees is coarser and it sits on fewer regime flips. That is why it is a genuinely different book rather than a re-tuned one. NOTE ON REGISTRATION: the HTF swing length is NOT an engine parameter, it is the registry's `swing` FIELD selecting a precomputed series, so this book needs the `htf15` series added to run_experiment.get_data - it is there, built at min_bars=15 on the 1h flow candles. A book that wanted a different HTF length would need its own series there, not a params edit. STILL NOT ADOPTED: period control gives b=+0.5681 IS and +0.3723 OOS, both positive with 97-98% of the raw gap surviving the half-year fixed effect, so it is not a regime proxy - but both cells are UNDERPOWERED against their own MDEs (1.0372 and 0.8050), so the magnitude is not established. In-sample drawdown rises 13.42R -> 17.28R and OOS 11.88R -> 16.86R, which fits the owner's 29R budget but is a real cost. And the OOS window is 2021-22, which is not a holdout - see method/OOS_IS_NOT_A_HOLDOUT.md. See method/HTF_SWEEP_OWNER_RULE.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mcloff
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - and the best-EVIDENCED one in the registry. It changes ONE INTEGER: max_consecutive_losses from 3 to 0, which turns the loss-run cutoff OFF. The autopsy of the parent's negative half-year found 2025-H1 was not a disaster but a coin flip that landed red: 60 trades, net -0.69R, mean -0.011R per trade, 20 winners making +29.6R against 40 losers making -30.3R. In that exact situation the cutoff is not protecting the book, it is cutting winners - it stops the book right before the recovery trade that follows every streak. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 575t / +566.58R / DD 15.13R / WR 39.7%, OOS 337t / +270.91R / DD 14.16R / WR 37.1%. IT DOMINATES THE PARENT ON RETURN IN BOTH ERAS (+33.21R IS, +31.32R OOS) on 47 and 26 MORE trades, for 1.71R and 2.28R of extra drawdown. ZERO negative half-years out of 12. PERIOD CONTROL IS THE REASON TO TRUST IT - this is the only arm in the whole family whose effect is SIGN HOLDS and POWERED in BOTH eras: b = +1.21 (t = 3.37, MDE 0.70) IS and b = +1.86 (t = 3.97, MDE 0.92) OOS, cluster-bootstrap b_boot +1.28 and +1.92. Compare fsent_champ_long_htf15 (underpowered), fsent_champ_long_biasmom05 (b NEGATIVE and significant at t = -9.63 OOS) and htf_fs=all (underpowered). Still NOT adopted: the period control compares this arm to champ_long, NOT to absolute zero, and a book that is meaningfully better than its parent can still be negative in some unseen half-year. The cutoff also has a real purpose under position sizing, which is a risk decision and not a signal decision. Forward evidence does not exist for it yet. See method/MAXCONSEC_LOSSES_FINDING.md. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0312 in sample, p = 0.0117 out of sample, gap +33.22 IS and +31.32 OOS - the only book in the family significant in BOTH eras. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.

books.name: fsent_sig_multi_htffs
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the best risk profile of the three FS-entered arms and it still fails the owner's rule on the negative cell. fsent_sig_multi with exp_htf_fs_entry='flip'. MEASURED: IS 434t / +666.32R / DD 17.82R / WR 45.2%, OOS 220t / +234.48R / DD 7.99R / WR 46.8%. Out-of-sample drawdown 7.99R and win rate 46.8% are the best numbers on this entry anywhere in the family, and the period control is positive (b = +0.42 at t = +1.81 half-year, better in 3 of 6 years) though the weakest of the three. WHY IT IS NOT THE PICK: it adds a negative half-year that sig_multi does not have - sig_multi is one of only two books in this family with ZERO negative cells, and this arm gives that up. Trading the single best-behaved shape in the family for a wider one is a bad exchange at this ratio, and the owner does not trade there. Registered with that named, because the out-of-sample numbers on it are the best in the family and the reason they are not adopted is not that they are bad - it is that the rule they break is the one the book was chosen for. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.5091 in sample, p = 0.9708 out of sample, gap +132.95R IS and -5.11R OOS - NOT significant in either era, and the out-of-sample gap is NEGATIVE. Worth being blunt about the ordering here, because the risk numbers point the other way: this arm has the best out-of-sample drawdown (7.99R) and the best out-of-sample win rate (46.8%) anywhere in the family, and it is the one whose edge is least distinguishable from its parent. Good risk profile is not evidence of edge, and a book can be quietly pleasant to hold and still be indistinguishable from reshuffling its parent's trades.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mode_atr_low
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - blocked on drawdown against the owner's 20R budget, not on the invented 11.88R gate (withdrawn 2026-10-08 as mine, not the framework's). fsent_champ_long with mode='atr_low' - the atr_high inversion: decisive windows when 15m bars are QUIET, not big. Only the mode changes; every other knob identical. This is the strongest of the four on the framework's own buckets: it WINS bucket 1 outright in both eras - IS 641t / +721.3R / expectancy 1.125 / PF 3.22 against the base 528t / +533.4R / 1.010 / 3.09, and OOS 315t / +280.7R / 0.891 / 2.96 against 311t / +239.6R / 0.770 / 2.69 - on MORE trades than the base, so more evidence and not less. Its out-of-sample tail is also the healthiest in the set (top 5% contributes 71.2% against the base's 81.1%; removing the top 10% still leaves -4.6% against -11.7%; removing the top 5% leaves 26.3% against 16.3%) and its DD expansion is 0.51, i.e. half its out-of-sample drawdown is in-sample. It is blocked purely on bucket 2 and bucket 9: 28.9R max DD in sample against the owner's 20R budget, 82 trades to make the drawdown, 460 trades underwater against the base's 286, and a 16-trade losing streak against the base's 11. Its own threshold swept 0.20-0.60 and the OOS gain peaks sharply at 0.35 (+41.1R) and is NEGATIVE everywhere else - one point, not a region, which is exactly the grid-peak failure P69 warns about. This is the one candidate worth keeping open, and the open question is whether a 20R budget can stretch to 29R - the owner's call, not the registry's. See method/OWNER_SCORECARD_MODES.md.

books.name: fsent_sig_sw20_short
books.desc: SERIAL signal book on the sw20 chain, SHORTS enter at swing FS PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0177 in sample, p = 0.1570 out of sample, gap -114.86 IS and -57.58 OOS - significant with a NEGATIVE gap: the swap is reliably WORSE than the parent, which is a real result and not an endorsement. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.
